title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — justification scope prefers Adam's actual
pass_a_gloss: GAR: Paul treats justification's cause, not sanctification's—so no wonder if primarily he means Adam's actual rather than inhering corruption: Adam's deed and the reatus from it answer Christ's righteousness and our justification by it; internal corruption answers rather the holiness inhering by the Spirit. Corruption may be folded in by the link we named, yet it is not Paul's direct aim here—he will treat it openly later.
pass_b_english: GAR. Since the Apostle here treats the cause of justification, not of sanctification, it is no wonder if from his primary intention he wished here rather to look at Adam's actual sin than at that inhering corruption, since the sin committed by Adam, and the reatus following from it, answers to the righteousness of Christ, and to our justification through it: but internal corruption answers not properly to that righteousness of Christ, but rather to the holiness inhering in us through the Holy Spirit. Which corruption, although here also because of that connection we have named it can be comprehended, yet does not directly regard the Apostolic aim, as in what follows Paul will treat of it openly.
source_text: GAR. Cum causam justificationis, non sanctificationis hic tractet Apostolus, nihil mirum est, si ex primaria sua intentione hic potius peccatum actuale Adami, quam corruptionem illam inhaerentem spectare voluerit, cum peccatum ab Adamo patratum, reatus ex illo consequens, respondeat justitiae Christi, & justificationi per eam nostrae: corruptio vero interna, non illi Christi justitiae proprie, sed potius inhaerenti per Spiritum Sanctum in nobis sanctitati respondeat. Qua corruptio quanquam hic etiam propter illam quam diximus connexionem comprehendi potest, non tamen Apostolicum scopum directe respicit, sicut in sequentibus de illa aperte agetur a Paulo.

choices.choice: Paul aims justification → actual answers Christ's justice
